To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sequence dependence in post‐tetanic facilitation of field potentials was abolished in the presence of atropine, but not in the presence of pirenzepine.
the sequence dependence in the induction of post‐tetanus potentiation in the auditory cortex might have a role as the temporal processing of the auditory information on the time scale of seconds.

post‐tetanic potentiations (PTPs) were induced in excitatory postsyaptic potentials (EPs) in rat auditory cortex (AC) slices after tetanic stimulation (T) was sequentially applied to two sites at intervals of 5–10 seconds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms for the processing of stimulus sequence in the AC, which may have a role in temporal coding of the stimulus.
the mechanism of sequence dependence of PTF and LTP in the rat AC.
the mechanisms for the sequence dependence of synaptic plasticity and the role in temporal processing of auditory stimuli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temporal sequence dependence of PPT in AC is a function of the temporal sequence dependence on M1 receptor activation.
PTP is a sequence‐dependent form of plasticity, and that this sequence dependence may have a role in auditory processing.
the sequence‐dependence of PTP in the AC is mediated by M1 receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sequence dependence is induced in the supragranular layer of the auditory cortex, and the induction is mediated by M1 receptor‐dependent presynaptic facilitation.
the sequence‐dependent PPT and LTP in the auditory cortex might be mediated by muscarinic M2 receptors and the sequence‐dependent Ca2+ influx into the dendritic spines.
sequence‐dependent PPF in AC might be a mechanism for coding stimulus sequence in AC, and the mechanism might be mediated by muscarinic M2 receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PTP is a form of synaptic plasticity that is sequence dependent.
sequence‐dependent plasticity in the auditory cortex is dependent on the muscarinic M _{1} receptors.

the sequence of stimulation is important for the induction of long‐lasting potentiation of synaptic transmission, and the underlying cellular mechanisms may be mediated by the activation of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors in the auditory cortex of rats.
